projectTitle: Robert Rauschenberg Foundation: Drupal 7 to 10 Website Migration
project_haiku:
Art lives beyond time
Digital archives preserve
Creative spirit soars
project_footer_CTA: Ready to preserve and celebrate artistic legacy through digital innovation? Let's create something timeless.
pageSummary:
Client background

The Robert Rauschenberg Foundation (RRF) is a non‑profit founded by the artist Robert Rauschenberg in 1990. A pioneering figure in post‑war art, Rauschenberg served in the U.S. Navy before studying at the Kansas City Art Institute, the Académie Julian in Paris and Black Mountain College, and he moved to New York in 1949 where he challenged artistic conventions with his Combinesrauschenbergfoundation.org. Today the Foundation builds on his legacy and emphasizes his belief that artists can drive social changerauschenbergfoundation.org. The organization supports programs and residencies and stewards an extensive archive that preserves the most comprehensive body of information on Rauschenberg's life and careerrauschenbergfoundation.org, making it both a cultural authority and a philanthropic institution of international prestigerauschenbergfoundation.org.

Project goals and challenges

By 2024 the Foundation's public website had grown into a complex Drupal 7 platform with dozens of content types and views. Non‑technical staff found it difficult to manage because many pages were entirely built using Views and custom templates. The site hosted more than a thousand artwork records, hundreds of archive entries and a wide range of program pages and timelines, much of which was entered through a FileMaker database. The team identified several key goals:

  • Modernize the CMS. Move from Drupal 7 to Drupal 10 to ensure long‑term support, improve security and leverage modern editing tools.
  • Simplify content management. Consolidate multiple basic‑page content types and heavy Views into a smaller set of flexible blocks so that non‑developers could update pages via Drupal 10's Layout Builder.
  • Integrate the FileMaker database. Use the Feeds FileMaker Module to import artwork and archive records. The existing FileMaker integration raised questions about whether artwork nodes should remain editable in Drupal or only in FileMaker and which fields could be eliminated.
  • Improve user experience. Preserve the ability to filter and search artworks and archives while streamlining navigation. Migrate specialized pages—such as the chronology, exhibition history and lightboxes—and consider richer visualizations such as an interactive timeline.
  • Consolidate mapping pages. On View and Public Collections pages both displayed works on maps via Pin Collection nodes; the new site needed to combine them into a single map with filterable pins while retaining the lists underneath.

Approach

Architecture and content strategy

A comprehensive content audit catalogued all Drupal 7 content types, views and templates. The audit recommended manually migrating simple pages and scripting the migration of large datasets such as artworks, series and archive entries. Content types such as Basic Page Centered, Basic Page Left Justified and Landing Page were consolidated into a single Basic Page to reduce complexity. The team also proposed using tile blocks and featured blocks to replace ad‑hoc views and create a consistent visual language for programs and collaborations pages.

Drupal 10 and Layout Builder

Drupal 10's Layout Builder gave non‑technical editors control over page composition. On the new home page, hero images, captions and introductory text became editable blocks instead of being buried in views. News items remained automatically generated by date but were exposed as a block that editors could reorder. The artwork, artist and programs sections were similarly transformed into layout‑builder sections, making the old Homepage Sections content type obsolete.

FileMaker integration via Feeds

Artwork and archive records originated from the Foundation's FileMaker database. To avoid manual data entry, the team used the Feeds FileMaker Module to connect Drupal 10 to the FileMaker PHP API, retrieve records and map fields to Drupal entities. The migration plan raised critical questions about which fields to retain and whether to allow edits in Drupal or force changes in FileMaker. The solution was to import core descriptive metadata (titles, dates, medium, credit lines) from FileMaker while adding a small number of Drupal‑only fields for features like exhibitions or notes that curators wanted to edit directly. Feeds setups were configured to run automatically on a schedule, ensuring that new or updated artworks and archives appeared on the site without manual intervention. A similar approach was taken for Series and Lightbox entities, allowing future automation based on FileMaker's series field.

Search, filtering and mapping

The artwork and archive search pages remained Views because they needed sophisticated filtering by medium, year and category. Drupal 10's Search API and Facets modules were used to replace older custom search code. For the On View and Public Collections pages, the team combined the two maps into a single map component with filterable pins; different colors indicated whether a work was currently on view or part of a public collection.

Chronology and exhibition history

The existing chronology page concatenated Chronology Section nodes into a long two‑column list, which was cumbersome for visitors and editors. The team evaluated modules like Views TimelineJS and external services such as Knight Lab's Timeline to build an interactive timeline that allows visitors to scroll through key events and search within the timeline. Exhibition history and performance history pages, previously built as Book Pages, were converted to Basic Pages with tertiary navigation items for easier management.

Programs and residencies

Program and residency pages were turned into Basic Pages with reusable blurb blocks. For example, the residencies landing page originally built with a Landing Page content type became a basic page where editors could add blurbs highlighting the Rauschenberg Residency on Captiva, the Archives Research Residency and the Rauschenberg Residency 381. Subpages like the chef‑in‑residence program and site history were migrated manually and organized using secondary navigation.

Outcomes

The new site delivered a streamlined editing experience and a more engaging presentation of the Foundation's collections and programs. Editors now manage hero images, news blocks and feature tiles through an intuitive drag‑and‑drop interface, eliminating the need to edit complex views. Automated imports from FileMaker ensure that the art and archive sections remain up to date without manual intervention. Consolidating content types and simplifying navigation reduce maintenance overhead and make it easier for users to find information. The combined On View/Public Collections map offers visitors a single point of entry to discover where Rauschenberg's works are exhibited worldwide, while the planned interactive timeline will bring his chronology to life. By migrating to Drupal 10 and leveraging modern modules like Feeds, Layout Builder and Search API, the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation has positioned its website to support its mission—promoting Rauschenberg's artistic and philanthropic legacyrauschenbergfoundation.org—for years to come.

In summary

In summary, the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation's move from Drupal 7 to Drupal 10 aimed to simplify content management, improve performance, and integrate a FileMaker database using the Feeds FileMaker module. The team consolidated numerous legacy content types into a single Basic Page format and adopted Layout Builder to empower non-developers with drag-and-drop page construction. Complex Views were retained only where advanced filtering was essential, such as for the searchable artwork and archive sections.

The integration with FileMaker automates the import of art and archive records while allowing select fields to be editable in Drupal, ensuring data integrity and curatorial flexibility. Navigation improvements include merging separate On View and Public Collections maps into a single, filterable map and converting the chronology into an interactive timeline. Overall, the project delivers a more intuitive user experience and positions the Foundation's digital presence to support its mission of promoting Rauschenberg's artistic and philanthropic legacyrauschenbergfoundation.org.
